installation.note: mkdir is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: mkdir (make directory) creates new directories in the filesystem. It can create single directories or multiple directories, and with the -p flag, can create parent directories as needed.

syntax.description: Create the specified directory(ies). Multiple directories can be created at once. Parent directories can be created automatically with -p.

misconceptions.title: mkdir -p creates a directory named -p
misconceptions.misconception: -p is part of the directory name
misconceptions.reality: -p is a flag that tells mkdir to create parent directories. The directory name comes after the flags.
misconceptions.tip: mkdir -p dir creates 'dir', not '-p'. The -p is an option flag, not part of the name.

misconceptions.title: mkdir can create files
misconceptions.misconception: mkdir creates files if given a filename
misconceptions.reality: mkdir only creates directories. Use touch or a text editor to create files.
misconceptions.tip: mkdir for directories, touch for files, or use text editors like nano/vim

misconceptions.title: mkdir needs full path
misconceptions.reality: mkdir works with both relative and absolute paths. Use relative paths from your current location, or absolute paths from root (/).
misconceptions.tip: mkdir dir creates in current directory. mkdir /path/to/dir uses absolute path.

common_pitfalls.description: Trying to create nested directory structure without -p flag
common_pitfalls.solution: Always use -p when creating directory paths with multiple levels: mkdir -p path/to/new/dir. Without -p, mkdir fails if parent directories don't exist.

common_pitfalls.description: mkdir fails if directory already exists
common_pitfalls.solution: Use mkdir -p to avoid errors if directory exists. The -p flag makes it idempotent (safe to run multiple times).

common_pitfalls.description: Directory names with spaces cause mkdir to create multiple directories
common_pitfalls.solution: Quote directory names with spaces: mkdir 'My Directory' or mkdir "My Directory". Or escape spaces: mkdir My\ Directory.

common_pitfalls.description: Cannot create directory in protected location
common_pitfalls.solution: Use sudo if you need to create directories in system locations. Or create in your home directory where you have permission.

best_practices: Always use -p when creating nested directory structures
Use -p for idempotent scripts (safe to run multiple times)
Use -m to set specific permissions when creating directories
Use -v for verbose output to see what's being created
Quote directory names with spaces: mkdir 'My Directory'
Use mkdir -p in scripts to avoid errors if directories already exist
Verify directory creation with ls after mkdir
Create directory structure before copying files into them
performance_tips: mkdir is very fast - creates directories instantly
Creating multiple directories at once is faster than one by one
Using -p is efficient for creating nested structures
mkdir -p is idempotent - safe and fast to run multiple times in scripts

additional_notes.directory_only: mkdir only creates directories, not files. Use touch or text editors for files.
additional_notes.parent_creation: The -p flag creates all parent directories automatically - very useful for nested structures
additional_notes.idempotent: mkdir -p is idempotent - safe to run multiple times without errors if directories exist
additional_notes.permissions: Default permissions are usually 755. Use -m to specify different permissions.
additional_notes.spaces: Always quote directory names with spaces to avoid creating multiple directories
additional_notes.scripting: mkdir -p is commonly used in scripts to ensure directory structure exists before operations
